key_insight: NLP on EHR notes uncovered symptom-based motor neuron disease subgroups that go beyond onset-site labels and align with different survival patterns.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help clinicians better stratify prognosis and tailor supportive care by identifying high-burden respiratory/autonomic phenotypes and a lower-risk sensory-pain phenotype.
method: Used MedCAT to extract symptom mentions from free-text clinical notes in 2,361 confirmed MND patients.
Filtered concepts to UMLS Sign/Symptom terms and removed negated findings.
Clustered binary symptom profiles with latent class analysis and tested survival with Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, and Cox models.
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 872 patients in the first-notes cohort and 2,065 patients across all notes, finding significant survival differences across symptom clusters (log-rank p < 0.001).
watch_item: Because this is a single-center retrospective NLP study, symptom coding quality, missing documentation, and external generalizability may limit immediate real-world use.
paper_title: Symptom-based phenotype discovery in motor neuron disease using natural language processing of electronic health records
